newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spanish government bonds ended lower on Friday, disheartened by U.S. data despite the presentation of a strict and realistic Spanish budget for 1998.
"The (U.S.) numbers are what kicked off the sales of bonds, but it seems that the guidelines of the 1998 budget have given the market some support," an analyst said.

The government pledged to lower the deficit to 2.4 percent of GDP from a projected 3.0 percent this year, in part through an expected acceleration of growth to 3.4 percent. Economists called the growth figures realistic and perhaps a bit modest.

"From the point of view of the market, the effect of the budget was relatively limited because some of the data had already been announced," said Valentin Fernandez, economist at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.

But the market suffered from U.S. July jobs and the National Association of Purchasing Managers data, with non-farm jobs well above expectations and a sharp unexpected jump in the prices component of NAPM.
The NAPM prices index rose to 53.6 in July from 48.1 in June, the first rise since February. Non-farm jobs grew by 316,000 compared with a forecast for 193,000.
